summary.intent: Use the GSD manager to discuss, plan, and begin executing phases 42 (API unpin integrity), 43 (FUSE write durability), and 44 (IPNS conflict handling) for the cipher-box project.
summary.outcome: All three phases were discussed and CONTEXT.md files committed; Phase 42 was fully planned (8 plans) and Wave 1 executed (plans 42-01 and 42-02 merged back to main branch with passing post-merge build/test gates).

repo: The unpin endpoint (POST /ipfs/unpin) is guarded only by JwtAuthGuard with no ownership check — the handler never reads req.user and passes any CID string directly to Kubo pin/rm, making cross-tenant data destruction possible with any valid JWT.

Kubo runs with the 'server' profile (docker/docker-compose.staging.yml:62-72) which keeps full public DHT participation and exposes swarm port 4001 publicly — all pinned CIDs are harvestable by DHT crawlers even though blobs are encrypted.
All current callers silently ignore unpin errors: web uses .catch(logger.warn), FUSE uses 'let _ =', so no client breaks on unpin failure — but errors are swallowed rather than surfaced.
Writable-share saves drop prunedCids without issuing any unpin call (shared-write.ts:450), meaning BYO-IPFS and shared-write flows have no unpin wiring at all.

eslint already ignores .planning and .claude directories, but .prettierignore did not exist, causing prettier to reformat markdown tables in planning files and corrupt regex patterns (pipe chars treated as table column separators).

The dedup content-addressing path (upload-compensation at ipfs.controller.ts:122) can fire a global pin/rm on a CID shared between multiple users, creating a cross-user unpin vector even without malicious intent.

IPNS records are published to the public IPFS network for TEE republishing and recovery — anyone observing an IPNS name can resolve it to the current metadata CID, providing another CID-discovery vector.

The FUSE write path has two known durability bugs: data loss if the process dies between local kernel cache flush and remote IPFS commit, and mkdir parent publishing orphan on concurrent directory creation.
Metadata CIDs from vault blob uploads and IPNS publishes are not tracked in pinned_cids rows, meaning a full pin/pinned_cids reconciliation sweep would flag these as orphans incorrectly.

code.finding: Kubo v0.40 configured with 'server' profile and swarm port 4001 exposed publicly (tcp+udp). Server profile only disables local-network discovery, not public DHT — every pinned CID is broadcast via provider records to DHT crawlers.
Upload-compensation path calls global Kubo pin/rm without any per-user ownership check — can unpin a content-addressed CID that another user's file deduplicates against.
Web client swallows all unpin errors with .catch(logger.warn) — callers never observe failure, making silent 2XX no-op the correct API contract for the no-row case.
FUSE write path has a durability window: data flushed to kernel cache but not yet committed to remote IPFS is lost on process crash. No crash-recovery journal or WAL exists today.
SDK folder operations lack IPNS conflict detection — concurrent writes from multiple devices can produce divergent IPNS chains with no merge or last-write-wins resolution.

workflow: GSD manager runs plan and execute inline on Claude Code (not as background agents) because backgrounded agents on Claude Code cannot nest the plan-checker or worktree-isolated executors that the pipelines rely on.
Wave-based execution uses isolated git worktrees per plan subagent; worktrees are merged back and removed after each wave via a manifest-tracked cleanup helper with a base_mismatch safety check.
TDD gate is enforced per plan: RED commit (failing tests) must precede GREEN commit (implementation); deviations require explicit justification in the plan SUMMARY.
Creating .prettierignore at repo root is necessary to prevent prettier from corrupting markdown planning files — pipe characters in code examples get interpreted as table column separators.
1Password SSH signing causes intermittent git commit failures on the first attempt requiring a retry; this is expected behavior in the local signing flow, not a git bug.
Silent git commit failures (HEAD not advancing) can occur when the pre-commit hook or signing prompt is dismissed — always verify HEAD after committing planning files.

friction: Session token limit hit mid-discussion of Phase 42, forcing the user to repeat their last message to resume.

AI repeatedly presented option menus instead of directly answering the user's explicit questions about unpin endpoint exposure and CID discoverability — required explicit correction ('you did not answer my question').
git commits silently failed (HEAD unchanged) multiple times across phases 42, 43, and 44 without surfacing an error — required manual log inspection and retry loops.
1Password SSH signing caused commit failures requiring a wait-and-retry cycle; the mechanism is opaque and the retry prompt appeared without clear guidance.
prettier reformatted regex patterns inside markdown planning files as table columns before .prettierignore was created, corrupting test command syntax in 42-VALIDATION.md.
Wave 1 worktree cleanup output was partially hidden, requiring manual branch/worktree state inspection before confirming both worktrees were actually merged and removed.
